---
title: "Published studies as diagrams"
description: "Ten published interference-control studies written as Studyflow diagrams from their articles alone, with each value an article does not state written as unstated."
---

Writing a study as a Studyflow diagram gives each of its decisions a place, so a decision that a description leaves out becomes visible. To see what this looks like for single studies, we rewrote ten published interference-control studies as Studyflow diagrams from their articles alone, without their supplements, code, or the papers they cite. Five used the Flanker task[^eriksen], four the Simon task[^simon], and one the Stroop task[^stroop]. They were published between 2010 and 2023 and include laboratory and online studies, a comparison of patients with healthy controls, a standardized test battery, a preregistered experiment, and studies of test-retest reliability (@tbl-encoded). Each diagram holds the same 20 values that a replication needs. Fifteen are settings of the task, such as the order of trials, the timing of a trial, and what happens when no response comes in time. The other five are the software that presented the task, the sample, the rules that excluded participants and trials, and the software of the analysis. Each value a diagram states is taken from the article, and each value the article does not state is written unstated, so the diagram is complete in form while its gaps stay visible. The passage of the article behind each stated value is recorded beside its diagram ([Files](#files)). All ten diagrams pass `studyflow validate` (release 26.11.2).

The articles stated between 10 and 17 of the 20 values (median 15.5). None stated the random seed of its trial order, seven did not name the software of the analysis, and five did not state a rule for excluding participants. Each is a decision a replication has to make again. The values that the articles did state were also spread across the text. Five articles gave the rule for selecting trials only in their Results, and two showed parts of a trial only in a figure.

Some of the unstated values may be stated in supplements, code, or an instrument's manual that we did not consult, so the diagrams measure what the articles alone specify. Audited the same way, the diagram of the example study of the Studyflow paper states all 20 values.

: Ten published interference-control studies written as Studyflow diagrams from their articles alone, and the example study of the Studyflow paper audited the same way. Each diagram holds the same 20 values that a replication needs, and each value that an article does not state is written `unstated`. {#tbl-encoded}

Taken together, these studies suggest that the gaps follow less from careless authors than from describing a process in prose, where nothing marks a decision as missing and nothing keeps the copies of a decision in agreement. Studyflow gives each decision a place in one diagram, which makes a missing value easy to see, and every view reads that one diagram.

## Files

Each study has a diagram and a quote record. The quote record gives, for each of the 20 values, the words of the article it was read from and where they stand, or why the value is unstated. [`check_encodings.py`](assets/examples/published-studies/check_encodings.py) checks every quote against the article's text on PubMed Central and each diagram against its record, and counts what the articles state.
